AI Startup SuperMe Secures $20 Million to Scale Expert Knowledge Network

Overview of SuperMe

SuperMe, a startup focused on creating a network of AI profiles modeled after real-world experts, has announced it successfully raised $20 million in a funding round. The investment was led by Forerunner’s Kirsten Green with participation from Greylock Partners. Founded in 2024 by industry veterans Casey Winters and Ludo Antonov, the company aims to democratize access to niche professional expertise.

How the Platform Functions

The platform operates by allowing users to pose career or technical questions to an AI-driven interface. The system matches the user's query with a group of relevant expert AI profiles.

  • Knowledge Aggregation: SuperMe pulls information from public sources, including LinkedIn, YouTube, Substack, and blogs. It also integrates with personal productivity tools like Google Drive, Notion, Gmail, and meeting assistants such as Granola.
  • Privacy Measures: While the system processes personal data and potential trade secrets from connected accounts, the company claims it has implemented safeguards to ensure this sensitive data is not exposed in the AI-generated responses.
  • Integration: The platform supports the Model Context Protocol (MCP), enabling users to interact with SuperMe’s expert models directly from other chatbot interfaces like Claude and ChatGPT.

Future Development and Business Model

Currently, the SuperMe service is free to use, though the founders have indicated plans to introduce usage caps and a fee-based model in the future. The company is actively hiring to bolster its technical team for model improvement and to expand its network of experts.

Investors, such as Forerunner’s Kirsten Green, highlighted the potential for the platform to foster human-AI collaboration. The founders intend to continue refining how the platform balances the sharing of insights with the need for data privacy and expert incentives.

Verifying the Announcement

To confirm the details of this funding round, readers are encouraged to consult official press releases issued directly by the startup or the lead investment firms. Independent verification of platform capabilities and privacy practices can typically be found within the company's service documentation and terms of use.
